claims.claim: The blog quotes a purported timeline entry saying Levi’s mother called his friend’s parents at 7:30 a.m. Oct. 23.

claims.claim: The blog quotes a purported timeline saying relatives found the bicycle, took it to the mother’s house and decided to return it before police arrived, within a 7:50 a.m. entry.

claims.notes: BATCH-MD-001; We do not possess the cited original GBI timeline or Nov. 3, 2004 newspaper reproduction. Do not infer intent from the described handling.

claims.claim: An unnamed law-enforcement officer is quoted by the blog as asserting no fingerprints remained on the bicycle and saying it had been wiped clean. The officer’s basis and forensic report are unavailable.
claims.assessment_rationale: Assessment concerns source attribution, not independent proof. Secondary-source chain is retained; machine-assisted, pending human review.
claims.notes: BATCH-MD-001; Not a confirmed forensic finding and not an inference concerning who handled the bicycle.

claims.claim: The blog’s purported timeline quotation places the mother’s missing-person report at 8 a.m. Oct. 23.
claims.assessment_rationale: Assessment concerns source attribution, not independent proof. Secondary-source chain is retained; machine-assisted, pending human review.
claims.notes: BATCH-MD-001;

claims.claim: The blog quotes a timeline entry placing the mother’s call to boyfriend Tim Tatum at his work at 9:30 a.m., followed by his departure for the search scene.
claims.assessment_rationale: Assessment concerns source attribution, not independent proof. Secondary-source chain is retained; machine-assisted, pending human review.
claims.notes: BATCH-MD-001;

claims.claim: The blog quotes a timeline entry saying Levi’s mother contacted the father about the situation at 10:15 a.m.
claims.assessment_rationale: Assessment concerns source attribution, not independent proof. Secondary-source chain is retained; machine-assisted, pending human review.
claims.notes: BATCH-MD-001;

claims.claim: The blog quotes a purported timeline placing discovery of Levi’s body at 2 p.m. Oct. 23 and reporting three shots.
claims.assessment_rationale: Assessment concerns source attribution, not independent proof. Secondary-source chain is retained; machine-assisted, pending human review.
claims.notes: BATCH-MD-001; A call time and a discovery time may differ; underlying timeline needed.

claims.claim: The blog attributes to unnamed Dawson and Forsyth authorities in 2014 an account of two head shots and one upper-body shot, not all fired at the same time or location.
claims.assessment_rationale: Assessment concerns source attribution, not independent proof. Secondary-source chain is retained; machine-assisted, pending human review.
claims.notes: BATCH-MD-001; No original autopsy, wound reconstruction or recorded interview acquired.

claims.claim: The same secondary account says Levi had called 911 in the days before his death; call dates, contents and records are not supplied.
claims.assessment_rationale: Assessment concerns source attribution, not independent proof. Secondary-source chain is retained; machine-assisted, pending human review.
claims.notes: BATCH-MD-001;

claims.claim: The blog quotes a letter attributed to Hendrix dated Sept. 2, 1998 alleging local investigators had not received requested scene photos and polygraph/interview information.
claims.assessment_rationale: Assessment concerns source attribution, not independent proof. Secondary-source chain is retained; machine-assisted, pending human review.
claims.notes: BATCH-MD-001; Underlying letter and distribution records not acquired; do not treat the blog as an official record.

claims.claim: The letter as quoted by the blog says a warrant for Marilyn Parkman’s home was executed without contemporaneous notice to Forsyth; a separate anonymous deputy claims a six-day delay.
claims.assessment_rationale: Assessment concerns source attribution, not independent proof. Secondary-source chain is retained; machine-assisted, pending human review.
claims.notes: BATCH-MD-001; Distinct letter assertion and anonymous timing assertion remain attributed; no actual warrant acquired.

claims.claim: The blog’s quoted Hendrix letter says Assistant District Attorney Jessica Moss told Forsyth officers to leave the Dawson scene, while Lt. Bill Miller was eventually allowed to view it.
claims.assessment_rationale: Assessment concerns source attribution, not independent proof. Secondary-source chain is retained; machine-assisted, pending human review.
claims.notes: BATCH-MD-001; Quoted allegation about agency access, not a proven official finding.

claims.claim: Hendrix is quoted as saying he believed a crime occurred in Forsyth County; this does not specify or prove that the homicide occurred there.
claims.assessment_rationale: Assessment concerns source attribution, not independent proof. Secondary-source chain is retained; machine-assisted, pending human review.
claims.notes: BATCH-MD-001; A crime could refer to a different act than the murder. Do not declare a geographic contradiction on this wording alone.

claims.claim: The blog quotes a Sept. 17, 1998 reply attributed to Nix stating intent to coordinate locally and extending Hallman’s apology for discomforts.
claims.assessment_rationale: Assessment concerns source attribution, not independent proof. Secondary-source chain is retained; machine-assisted, pending human review.
claims.notes: BATCH-MD-001;

claims.claim: The blog quotes Priscilla King’s June 6, 2016 email calling for an inquiry into handling of Levi’s case.
claims.assessment_rationale: Assessment concerns source attribution, not independent proof. Secondary-source chain is retained; machine-assisted, pending human review.
claims.notes: BATCH-MD-001; Expression of concern, not proof that the alleged irregularities occurred.

claims.claim: The blog places the family’s last sighting of Levi at 4:15 on Oct. 22; the text gives no explicit a.m./p.m. marker or identified witness for this precise clock reading.

claims.claim: The blog names Roman Martinez as a friend who reportedly watched Levi ride over a hill; no original Martinez interview is supplied.

claims.notes: BATCH-MD-001;

claims.claim: The blog attributes to an Oct. 24, 1997 AJC report a Wednesday-night bicycle sighting by Laci and Marilyn, but the paragraph also ends “Thursday (Oct. 23).” Its chronology is ambiguous.

claims.claim: In a blog-reported Feb. 18, 2016 phone interview, Kevin Tanner said nobody had come forward as someone who saw Levi being taken.

claims.claim: Tanner is quoted by the blog describing retired investigator Tim Attaway and FBI/GBI profilers as having worked the case.

claims.claim: The blog quotes Samples in a reported 2013 interrogation alleging that a “long gun” involved in his dispute was the one used on Levi; no original video or ballistic comparison is held.
claims.assessment_rationale: Assessment concerns source attribution, not independent proof. Secondary-source chain is retained; machine-assisted, pending human review.
claims.notes: BATCH-MD-001; Allegation only. Does not establish possession of a murder weapon or guilt of any individual.

claims.claim: The blog asserts records showed one warrant E0001481 for a knife, not a warrant for the alleged Frady gun, in the described 2013 incident.
